title: Forks: one move, two targets
outcomes: Explains why a fork wins material
Finds a knight fork that wins a queen when told to look for one
Checks whether a fork actually works before playing it

steps.text:
A **fork** is one move that attacks two things at once. Your opponent can answer only one threat, so you usually win the other piece.
Any piece can fork. Knights are the hardest to spot, because their jump attacks squares a bishop or rook line would not.

steps.caption: White to move. Watch what the knight does.

line.say: The knight jumps to c7 and attacks the king and the queen.
The knight takes the queen. White is a whole queen ahead.

steps.text:
Not every fork works. Before you jump, ask two questions:
**Can the forking piece be captured?**
**Is the second target worth taking?**
If the forking piece can simply be taken, the fork costs you the piece.

steps.title: Same idea, one change
steps.prompt: Black's king now stands on d8. Does Nc7 still win the queen? Predict first, then check.
Before you found the move: how sure were you that a fork existed? (low / medium / high)
